title: Unit and tower equations for the normalized finite Verdier comparisons
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D with field k and characteristic p, a prime l different from p, an algebraic closure Omega of Q_l in an independent universe, and a separated finite-type scheme X over k. Use the actual raw rational finite stages, scalar extensions, tensor comparisons and common-stage pair category of [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data]. For every Finite F of [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data], its specified beta maps satisfy FiniteCoherent: the actual stage-unit equation and actual associator equation, including repeated fields. Such normalized Finite data exist; finiteData_nonempty is the simultaneous rational Verdier construction with the finite Hom identifications.

source.place: Final coefficient-transport paragraph; core descent retained steps 1--5 and formal retract restriction step 10

proof.text: Obtain simultaneous rational Verdier data, choose integral dualizing presentations in the existential proof, and specialize the normalized extensions at the coefficient inclusions. Choose finite Hom identifications at the identity field map. Taking beta to be the scalar comparison makes betaNormalized reflexive. This is the preserved finite-data construction, with the original finite_data_exists theorem remaining a wrapper in the item.
Identify beta with the normalized rational scalar comparison using betaNormalized. Apply the rational unit and composition equations to the normalized extensions.

Identify the rationalized integral tensor unit and associator with the prescribed stage unitor and associator by their normalizations. The coefficient inclusions compose by their defining laws, so these equations are exactly FiniteCoherent, also when fields coincide.
